title: AI assistants
lead: Let an AI assistant read your hub's data and answer questions about your energy. The hub does the counting; the assistant reads the results. Nothing is open until you switch it on here.
directOnly: AI assistants are set up over a direct connection to the hub.
notOnThisHub: This hub doesn't offer an API for AI assistants.
loadFailed: Couldn't read the AI settings from the hub: {why}
enabledWarn: Paired assistants can read your energy data. With «propose changes» they can also suggest settings changes, which you confirm in the chat before anything is applied.
needAdminToken: Set an admin token first: until the hub has one, anyone on your network could read the pairing code.
readOnlyHint: Assistants may read but never change settings, whatever they were paired with.
pairNone: No assistant is asking to pair. Start pairing in the assistant; its code appears here.
pairHow: Read this code to the assistant in the chat. Only pair an assistant you started pairing yourself.
expired: Expired. Start pairing again in the assistant.
revokeBody: «{name}» will lose access to the hub at once. To use it again, pair it again.
connectWhenOn: Switch access on above to connect an assistant.
useIp: Use {url} instead (if «.local» names don't resolve on your computer)
desktop1: Install the RBgrid extension in Claude Desktop on the computer you chat on (that computer needs internet; the hub doesn't).
desktopSoon: The download link comes with the extension's release.
desktop2: Open the file: Claude Desktop installs it. Leave «Hub address» empty: the assistant finds the hub itself. Only if it can't (VPN, guest Wi-Fi, another subnet), enter {url}
sayConnect: Then in the chat say «connect to my RBgrid». The assistant asks for a 6-digit code: it appears on top of this app, on any page.
where_claude-code: Run this in a terminal on the computer where Claude Code runs:
where_cursor: Add this to Cursor's MCP settings (~/.cursor/mcp.json), then restart Cursor:
where_vscode: Add this to VS Code's MCP config (.vscode/mcp.json in the project, or «MCP: Open User Configuration»):
where_lmstudio: In LM Studio open Program → Install → Edit mcp.json and add:
where_other: Any MCP client that runs local servers: add this to its MCP config.
bridgeReadOnly: Only let this assistant read (the bridge refuses changes)
needsNode: Needs Node.js 18.19 or newer on that computer.
remoteTitle: Claude on the web or phone, ChatGPT
remoteBody: Through your own Cloudflare relay, without opening the hub to the internet. Coming in a later release.
haNote: Using Home Assistant? Its own MCP server can already read the RBgrid entities, so you don't need to pair the same assistant here too.
versionsLead: The hub keeps the settings an assistant can change — point names, roles and clamps, tariff prices, the peaks cycle day — as versions: the first one, from before any assistant change, and the newest 7. Any of them can be restored.
restoreNothing: The settings already match this version.
src_hub: the hub page or another app
eventsLead: The newest 20, the same list an assistant reads.
ev_price_missing: Dynamic prices missing: the plan price is used
bannerNoCode: An AI assistant wants to connect. Open AI assistants to see its code.
bridgeNotYetTitle: The RBgrid assistant bridge isn't published yet
bridgeNotYet: Assistants such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor reach the hub through a small bridge program on your computer. It isn't available for download yet; when it is, this card shows how to install it, with this hub's address filled in. The hub is ready: once an assistant asks to pair, its code appears on top of this app.
